question: How can a car chase filmed at a safe speed look terrifyingly fast on screen?
answer: By filming fewer frames each second. A camera running at 18 frames a second, played back at the standard 24, speeds everything up by a third; crews call it undercranking. Combined with a low camera close to the road and short, jumpy cuts, a careful drive becomes a race. Speed on screen is a setting.
move: Speed on a screen is a choice made by whoever filmed it.
